title: Penicillin: Discovery, Development, and Production
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
In 1928 Alexander Fleming observed that a mold contaminating a bacterial culture was associated with a clear zone where bacterial growth was inhibited. The contamination was accidental, but recognizing the pattern was not automatic. Fleming investigated the antibacterial substance and named it penicillin. Observation converted accident into a research question.

A promising effect in a dish is not yet a medicine. The active material was difficult to purify, unstable, and initially available only in small quantities. More than a decade later, a multidisciplinary Oxford team including Howard Florey, Ernst Chain, Norman Heatley, Edward Abraham, and others developed methods for extraction, purification, animal experiments, and early clinical use. Different steps required bacteriology, chemistry, engineering judgment, and clinical evaluation.

Scale created another problem. Producing enough penicillin for widespread treatment required fermentation research, improved strains and media, industrial equipment, government coordination, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. Work in Britain and the United States, including research at a U.S. agricultural laboratory, helped transform scarce experimental material into a mass-produced medicine. The causal chain cannot be reduced to either one scientist or one company.

Penicillin changed the treatment of susceptible bacterial infections, but “miracle drug” can hide limits. It does not treat viruses, not every bacterium is susceptible, adverse reactions occur, and selection favors resistant variants when antibiotics are used. The history therefore joins discovery with stewardship: a medical tool remains valuable only when its biological limits and social system of use are understood.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Accidental contamination alone created a finished medicine.

options.label: B
options.text: Penicillin became a medicine through linked stages of observation, development, production, and responsible use.

options.label: C
options.text: Penicillin is effective against every infectious agent.

options.label: D
options.text: Industrial production required no scientific research.

questions.answer: 正解：B。観察、開発、量産、責任ある使用の連鎖が主題です。Aは工程を消し、Cは適応を誇張し、Dは発酵・設備研究を無視します。

questions.prompt: Why was the discovery not merely an accident even though the contamination was accidental?

options.label: A
options.text: Fleming recognized the clear-zone pattern, investigated it, and turned it into a testable research question.

options.label: B
options.text: Every contaminated culture automatically becomes a medicine.

options.label: C
options.text: The mold was deliberately placed there as a finished drug.

options.label: D
options.text: No trained observation or follow-up was required.

questions.answer: 正解：A。偶発的汚染に意味を見いだし、再調査して検証可能な問いへ変えた判断が必要でした。B～Dは偶然と知識に基づく認識を混同します。

questions.prompt: The statement “Scale created another problem” means that

options.label: A
options.text: increasing quantity introduced new technical and organizational demands

options.label: B
options.text: researchers needed only a more accurate weighing scale

options.label: C
options.text: small experiments were already sufficient for all patients

options.label: D
options.text: the molecule became heavier during fermentation

questions.answer: 正解：A。実験量から社会的供給量へ増やす際の発酵、菌株、設備、組織の課題を指します。Bは語義の誤読、CとDは量産問題と異なります。

questions.prompt: Which set of steps was needed to move from a clear zone in a dish to a usable medicine?

options.label: A
options.text: Extraction and purification, stabilization and testing, clinical evaluation, and sufficient production

options.label: B
options.text: Naming the substance and immediately treating every patient

options.label: C
options.text: Observing the culture without isolating or testing the active material

options.label: D
options.text: Replacing bacteriology and chemistry with advertising

questions.answer: 正解：A。抽出・精製、安定化、動物実験、臨床評価、十分量の生産が必要でした。B～Dは有望な作用と安全で再現可能な薬を同一視します。

questions.prompt: Why can mass production not be credited to one company alone?

options.label: A
options.text: It linked strain and medium improvement, fermentation, equipment, government resources, manufacturing, and transatlantic knowledge transfer.

options.label: B
options.text: No government, laboratory, engineer, or manufacturer contributed.

options.label: C
options.text: Large-scale production required only Fleming's original culture dish.

options.label: D
options.text: Britain and the United States worked without sharing any knowledge.

questions.answer: 正解：A。菌株・培地、発酵、装置、政府調整、企業生産、英米の知識移転が連結しました。B～Dは多主体の因果連鎖を消します。

questions.prompt: Which inference is best supported by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Serendipity eliminates the need for trained observation.

options.label: B
options.text: Clinical promise and mass supply are separate questions.

options.label: C
options.text: Antibiotics treat viral infections if the dose is high enough.

options.label: D
options.text: Resistance makes every past use of penicillin worthless.

questions.answer: 正解：B。有望な薬効を示すことと広範に供給できることは別の問題です。Aは観察、Cは病原体、Dは価値と限界を取り違えます。

questions.prompt: Which limitation can the phrase “miracle drug” conceal?

options.label: A
options.text: Penicillin does not treat viruses, some bacteria are not susceptible, adverse reactions occur, and resistance can be selected.

options.label: B
options.text: Penicillin cures every infection without diagnosis, dose, or duration decisions.

options.label: C
options.text: All bacteria remain permanently susceptible under any use pattern.

options.label: D
options.text: The drug has no biological or social limits.

questions.answer: 正解：A。ウイルスへの無効性、非感受性菌、副反応、耐性選択などを隠し得ます。B～Dはまさに本文が退ける無制限な万能薬像です。

questions.prompt: What does “Observation converted accident into a research question” mean?

options.label: A
options.text: Recognition reframed a dismissible contamination as a phenomenon that could be investigated and tested.

options.label: B
options.text: Observation chemically changed the mold into a different substance.

options.label: C
options.text: The accident already contained a complete clinical and industrial program.

options.label: D
options.text: The clear zone was ignored as meaningless contamination.

questions.answer: 正解：A。物質変換ではなく、捨て得た汚染を検証可能な問題として捉え直した認識論的変化です。B～Dはconvertedの意味を誤ります。

questions.prompt: Which revision best corrects the claim that Fleming single-handedly invented penicillin as a medicine?

options.label: A
options.text: Fleming's observation was essential, while later teams, laboratories, governments, engineers, and manufacturers solved purification, testing, and production problems.

options.label: B
options.text: Fleming alone completed extraction, trials, fermentation, and worldwide manufacture in 1928.

options.label: C
options.text: The Oxford team made Fleming's observation irrelevant.

options.label: D
options.text: No scientist or institution contributed intentionally because the first event was accidental.

questions.answer: 正解：A。発見の重要性を保ちながら、精製・実験・臨床・量産を解決した多主体の貢献を示します。B～Dは単独英雄化か逆の消去です。
